name: Quince
description: Quince (Cydonia oblonga) is a structurally dense pome fruit characterized by a high pectin content and a robust polyphenolic antioxidant profile. Its unique botanical matrix—rich in organic acids and soluble fibers—is engineered to optimize gastrointestinal mucosal integrity, vascular elasticity, and systemic immune kinetics.
macroIntro: A clean, low-calorie carbohydrate framework providing high volumetric satiety with a near-zero lipid footprint, suitable for glycemic management.
microIntro: A functional micronutrient payload featuring Vitamin C and essential trace minerals that reinforce tissue structural integrity and metabolic defense mechanisms.

healthBenefits: Mucosal Gastroprotection: High concentrations of soluble pectin form a protective bio-gel over gastric linings, mitigating low-grade inflammation.
Astringent Antioxidant Defense: Polyphenolic tannins (catechins) actively precipitate and neutralize toxic metabolites, shielding the intestinal epithelium.
Vascular Elasticity: Synergistic Vitamin C and Copper profiles promote robust collagen cross-linking within capillary walls.
Hepatic Modulation: Organic acids and polyphenols assist in lipid metabolism, reducing oxidative stress within hepatic transport pathways.
precautionsIntro: Structural preparation and toxicity considerations regarding botanical processing:
precautions: Astringency & Digestion: High tannin content may irritate hyper-sensitive digestive tracts or cause oral mucosa dryness; thermal processing (poaching) is recommended.
Seed Toxicity: Quince seeds contain amygdalin (cyanogenic glycoside); the core must be removed entirely prior to consumption.
Culinary Glycemic Load: Commercial preserves (jams, pastes) are typically formulated with high sugar concentrations; monitor serving sizes to avoid glycemic spikes.
